title: Go: WaitGroup
description: Use sync.WaitGroup to wait for multiple goroutines to finish their work.

steps.title: Add/Done/Wait basics
steps.description: Launch a goroutine that prints "Task completed". Use `sync.WaitGroup` to wait for it to finish before main exits.
hints: Call `wg.Wait()` in main to block until Done is called

verification.successMessage: WaitGroup correctly waited for the goroutine!
verification.failureMessage: Make sure you call Add, Done, and Wait in the right places.

steps.title: Multiple goroutines
steps.description: Launch 5 goroutines using a WaitGroup. Each prints "Worker X done" (where X is 1-5). Main waits for all before printing "All workers finished".
hints: Call `wg.Add(5)` before the loop, or add inside the loop
Pass the WaitGroup pointer to the goroutine if wrapping in a function

verification.successMessage: All 5 workers completed before main exited!
verification.failureMessage: Use a loop to launch 5 goroutines with the WaitGroup.

steps.title: WaitGroup with work function
steps.description: Create a `worker(id int, wg *sync.WaitGroup)` function that prints "Worker X processing" and calls Done. Launch 3 workers and wait for all.
hints: The worker function must receive `wg *sync.WaitGroup` as a parameter
Call `defer wg.Done()` at the start of the worker
Always pass WaitGroup by pointer, never copy it

verification.successMessage: Workers with WaitGroup parameter pattern works!
verification.failureMessage: Your worker function must accept and call Done on the WaitGroup.

steps.title: Add inside a loop
steps.description: Process a slice of 5 URLs (use fake strings). For each URL, call `wg.Add(1)` then launch a goroutine that fetches (simulate with sleep) and prints "Fetched: <url>".
hints: Call wg.Add(1) inside the loop, before each goroutine
Be careful with closure capture — pass the url as a parameter

verification.successMessage: All URLs processed with concurrent fetches!
verification.failureMessage: Make sure wg.Add is called before each goroutine launch.

steps.title: WaitGroup reuse
steps.description: Use a single WaitGroup for two batches of work. First batch: 3 goroutines printing "Batch 1". Wait, then second batch: 2 goroutines printing "Batch 2". Print "All done" at the end.
hints: After first `wg.Wait()`, call `wg.Add(2)` for the second batch
WaitGroup counters can be reused — just Add again after Wait returns
This is useful for staggered work dispatches

verification.failureMessage: Add to the WaitGroup again after the first Wait completes.
